### W5. The declarations that the code generator refuses (rows 624, 81, 822, 812, 819, 315, 540, 875, 818)

Past W4, `FortressBuiltin` compiles whole. `FortressLibrary` stops at its first refused declaration ('Can't compile VarArgs yet', `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:307`). Section 3 counts them: 24 in 8 kinds, each kind in a row. Hack: the distance probe's tolerant code generator (`tools/distance/shadow-patch.py`'s edits of `CodeGen.java`) put into the scratch tree's `CodeGen`, so that a refused declaration is reported and left out and the jar is still written. That hack needed three repairs of its own, none of them a finding about the tree: a refused trait left its class writer in place of the component's, so the jar was never closed; a refused function left a half-written method, so each method is now kept apart until its class is written and one left open is written as a body that throws; and the wrapper generator writes its classes by another route, which had to flush the kept methods too.

Leaving a declaration out is enough only where nothing on a program's path needs it. Five refused declarations were on the path of a program that prints one line, and each needed a stub in the library's text (section 4).

### W6. One method written twice into a class (row 571's kind; 27 classes, 244 methods)

First load of the library:

    java.lang.ClassFormatError: Duplicate method name "MAX?0" with signature "(Lcom.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FZZ32;)Lcom.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FZZ32;" in class file fortress/FortressLibrary$ZZ32$DefaultTraitMethods

The code generator writes one name and descriptor twice into 24 classes of `FortressLibrary`'s jar (238 methods) and 3 of `RangeInternals`' (6 methods, `narrowToRange`). The compile reports nothing; each class fails when it loads. Row 571 holds one shape of it (an object that declares the meet of two inherited methods). The library's shape is wider: a trait that declares its own method at the instance of a generic supertrait's method, as `ZZ32`'s `<`, `MAX` and `CMP` beside `StandardPartialOrder[\ZZ32\]`'s and `StandardMinMax[\ZZ32\]`'s, gets a forwarder for each, under one name and descriptor. So the code generator does not see that the trait's own declaration overrides the inherited one.

The first hack, keep the first copy, ran `println` once and then, after an unrelated rebuild, sent it into a `StackOverflowError`: the copy kept for `ZZ32`'s `<` forwarded to `StandardPartialOrder`'s `<`, which calls `CMP`, which calls `<`. Which copy comes first is not stable from one compile to the next. The hack now prefers the copy that calls a static method of the class itself, the trait's own declaration: 98 of the 238 are swapped by that rule. A real repair: one rung at least, at the place where a trait's forwarders are gathered, with the override test at the instantiated signature; it first sorts the 244 by cause.

### W7. Missing casts that the JVM's verifier refuses (rows 307 and 695's kind; not counted)

      Location: fortress/FortressLibrary$QQ$DefaultTraitMethods.isFinite(Lfortress/FortressLibrary$QQ;)Lcom/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FBoolean; @1: invokestatic
      Reason: Type 'fortress/FortressLibrary$QQ' (current frame, stack[0]) is not assignable to 'fortress/FortressLibrary$Ratio'

`getter isFinite(): Boolean = (denominator(self) =/= 0)` in `trait QQ comprises { Ratio }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:570`): the checker lets `self` stand where the comprised object type `Ratio` is expected, and the code generator emits no cast. It is thrown from `FortressLibrary`'s static initializer, at the first numeral coercion into `QQ`, so it stops every program. In `QQ` alone 23 lines pass `self` to `numerator` or `denominator`. Rows 307 and 695 hold the kind for a program's own traits; no row names the library's `QQ`. Hack: every compiled run of this probe had the verifier switched off (`-XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions -XX:-BytecodeVerificationRemote`). So nothing below shows how many other methods the verifier refuses, and a count needs every emitted class loaded with the verifier on, which this probe did not build. A real repair: the cast where a value typed by a trait with a `comprises` clause meets a listed type (row 307's repair), one rung, and then the count.

        at Writer$stdOut.<clinit>(Library/Writer.fss:17)
        at fortress.FortressLibrary.println(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4709)

Row 624 is on every program's path: varargs must compile, or the library's text must change, before a line prints.

Behind `Generator2`'s `label` stands a second wall, 'Can't compile VarArgs yet', and behind `List`'s duplicate closure class likewise: a declaration counted at its first wall can hold more.

### W10. A closure class written twice into the jar (row 315's kind) stops `=` on two `ZZ32` values

    Caused by: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/FortressLibrary$LexicographicOrder$RTTIi
        at ...FortressLibrary⚙$CMP⟦FZZ32⟧...the_function
        at ...StandardPartialOrder⟦FZZ32⟧$DefaultTraitMethods.=(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:232)
        at ...Indexed⟦FCharacter,FZZ32⟧$DefaultTraitMethods.isEmpty(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2120)
        at fortress.FlatStringC$FlatString$DefaultTraitMethods.||(Library/FlatString.fss:126)

`trait LexicographicOrder` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2216-2228`) is refused, 'java.util.zip.ZipException: duplicate entry: FortressLibrary$\=fn@2227\!12-52??.class', and the dispatch method of `CMP` names every overload's trait, so comparing two integers needs its class. Hack: the jar writer keeps the first copy of a class. `List` has the same failure (`Library/List.fss:128`).

        at ...Array⟦FRR64,Tuple⟦FZZ32,FZZ32⟧⟧$DefaultTraitMethods._[_]:=(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2369)

`Array[\E,I\]` declares `offset(i:I): I` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2314`); `Array2` gives `offset(t1:(ZZ32,ZZ32)):(ZZ32,ZZ32)` (`:2847`). At `I = (ZZ32,ZZ32)` the abstract method takes one boxed tuple, and the body written at the tuple type was compiled with another descriptor, with no bridge between them. So `m[i,j] := x` and `m[i,j]` die on every rank-2 and rank-3 array, a `Matrix` among them. Row 832 holds the nearest shape (a generic dotted method whose single parameter has a tuple type from a tuple static argument). **No hack gets past it: it needs the code generator to emit the bridge, a rung's real work. The probe stops on this line here.**

### W16. The library's vector algebra: a generic method inherited from an api's trait has no body on the object (rows 495 and 732's kind)

    Caused by: java.lang.AbstractMethodError: Receiver class RangeInternals$CompactFullParScalarRange does not define or inherit an implementation of the resolved method 'abstract java.lang.Object map⟦…⟧(long, java.lang.String)' of interface fortress.FortressLibrary$Indexed⟦FZZ32,FZZ32⟧.
        at ...ReadableArray⟦FRR64,FZZ32⟧$DefaultTraitMethods.indexValuePairs(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2288)
        at ...FortressLibrary$fn@2716...apply(Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2716)
        at ...__bigOperator...

`a DOT b` on two `Vector[\RR64,1000\]` values reaches `Indexed`'s generic method `map[\R\]` on a range object of `RangeInternals`, which has no implementation of it: the object inherits the generic method's body from a trait of another component's api. PLAN's phase 4 names this arm ("an object's inherited generic method … dies at the generic arm", from the generic-`distribute` probe) and phase 5 names rows 495 and 496. **No hack was tried: it is the code generator's generic dotted methods, a rung's real work.** Every `map`, `ivmap` and `DOT` of microGPT's vocabulary is on it.

# (perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md, sections 1 and 3, whose run.sh and classify2.py were not kept): the

# add-patch.py), and its driver, DistanceMulti, run with -order full (every compiler phase, code generation among
# them) and -setting compile, the compile command's own setting, which the distance stage runs (its run.sh), over
# the stage's fourteen components in its order. The report's flags: -Dprobe.tolerant=true (the checker checks each
# declaration apart and its errors stop nothing; code generation catches each declaration's failure),
# -Dprobe.bottomCompare=true, -Dprobe.skipOverloads=true (no dispatch methods), the overloading memo off.

( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \

echo "rc=$? seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))" >> "$O/run.txt"

A numeral's conversion into its default (\secref{literals}) is not a coercion,

- P-169 **The runtime's own 13 native bindings, the arrays' store, threads with `abort` and the task trace, name compiled helpers that walk's loader answers with walk's own operations, P-167's device, in two compiled shapes.** Each keeps P-58's form, a bare `builtinPrimitive("…")` naming a helper of `nativeHelpers/` that the compiled path runs; walk's loader answers the name with walk's glue, so walk keeps its `AtomicArray` store and its `spawn`, and for these names P-58's walk half bends, as for P-167's two. The arrays' 7, of `PrimitiveArray`, `PrimImmutableArray` and `PrimImmutableRR64Array`: the compiled half by P-164's device, a store trait in `FortressLibrary` whose bindings name helpers of a new `nativeHelpers/arrayOps` over a compiled class that holds the elements; `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` leave the native component and hold the store in a field, and walk's native object below the trait holds an `AtomicArray`; `PrimImmutableRR64Array`'s two are on a compiled `double[]` class that no factory chooses until array decision A (P-84, P-85; F-333). The compiled store is an `Object[]`, and the compiled transaction tracks its reads and writes by the array and the index (`TXReadSlot`, `TXWriteSlot`): P-84 stores every number type's array unboxed, so a compiled `atomic` write into any array needs that keying, and an array of objects keeps one box an element, not two. Threads, `abort` and the task trace, 6: helpers in a `nativeHelpers` class over the compiled runtime, as the team's `nativeHelpers/runtime.java` is (F-335); `Thread`'s `val`, `wait`, `ready` and `stop` raise until the code generator compiles `spawn` (row 82). The numerals' 24 bindings, `IntLiteral`'s 21 and `FloatLiteral`'s 3, left the library with those two types (P-174), so no carrier is designed for them; `IntLiteral`'s other 8, its conversions and comparisons, left with it. A test on both paths holds the two halves together where both run. Why: every array, vector, varargs list and `args` of the one library is built on `PrimitiveArray` or `PrimImmutableArray`, and a body left on glue compiles to the library's own `builtinPrimitive`, which fails, so by the code's reading a compiled program would raise at its first array; walk's loader carries no element, `Thread` or literal (F-299), and an `Object` carrier would take walk's array writes out of walk's transactions. Detail: `reviews/natives-device-2026-11-07.md`, sections 3.1 to 3.4; the store's shape: `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md`, "The questions for the curator, before the launch", Q2.

- P-125 **The suites run Fortress in parallel, pinned at four threads in `build.xml`.** `build.xml` sets `FORTRESS_THREADS` to 4 for the two suites, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem`, so that every run of them uses four threads, whatever the calling shell sets. A test that parallelism makes fail, on every run or only on some, is written wrong, for example a write that needs `atomic`, or it shows a defect. Either is fixed, never hidden by running at one thread. Why: Fortress is parallel by default, so a suite at one thread has a blind spot, and sparing the four-CPU machine is no reason for one.

- F-351 **A compiled transaction validates itself and every ancestor, and an abort restarts the block whose transaction it names.** A compiled `atomic` block's transaction records no read of its own write; it records a read of an ancestor's write with that write, a read of the committed value with that value, and a read of an empty array element with a mark. Validation, at a read once the global lock has moved and at a commit that did not get the lock at its snapshot, covers the transaction and every ancestor. An abort names the transaction whose read failed; `abort()` names none. The block's handler takes every exception (`BaseTask.leaveTransaction`): it ends the block's transaction, starts the block again for an abort that names that transaction or names none (or any abort at the outermost block), and throws everything else on, after a nested transaction has handed its reads to its parent. A nested commit hands its parent its reads and its writes, also where it wrote nothing. The exception-table entry of a block or a `try` follows its body's code, so a nested one is taken first. Open: a nested block sees a plain write by another thread that runs its outer block (row 984). Source: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:228-367`, `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:293-314`,`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1835-1867` (`forAtomicBlock`), `:2169-2173` (`forTry`). Tests: `compiler_tests/AtomicOwnWriteNestedCompiled`, `AtomicNestedSameBodyCompiled`, `NestedAtomicAbortCompiled`, `AtomicNestedViewCompiled`, `AtomicSharedReadsCompiled`, `AtomicThrowRevertsCompiled`, `AtomicNestedReadsKeptCompiled`, `NestedTryInnerCatch`; `ArrayStoreJUTest`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-compiled-transaction/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

- P-175 **On the compiled path a call's arguments run in parallel where `ParallelismAnalyzer` judges them worth a task, as a tuple's elements do, so a reduction's two halves run in parallel; the one library's parallel range stops its split at a grain size, not at single elements.** The one library's range joins a reduction's halves as the arguments of one call, `red.join(loop'(lo, mid-1), loop'(mid, hi))`, and split down to single elements when the curator decided (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:1312-1350`); the code generator evaluated a call's arguments in order, under the team's comment "Why isn't this parallel???", so every `SUM`, `DOT` and `BIG MAX` of microGPT would have run its bodies one at a time once compiled programs ran the one library. The split stops at a chunk that runs efficiently in sequence: in his words, "you need the right forking constants", as Steele's parallel trees end in sequential leaves and Clojure's persistent vectors take their branching factor from B-trees. It needs a group of forked arms to join every arm before it completes abruptly, which the compiled path did not do (`CodeGen.genParallelExprs` joined on the normal path only; `reviews/parallelism-foundations-2026-11-08.md`, section 7.1); F-350 gives what it does now. The library binding the halves as a tuple, and reductions left in sequence, are declined. Why: the specification evaluates each argument of a call in an implicit thread of its own (`Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:60-64`), walk forks a call's arguments (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:342`), and the model's parallelism is its reductions (the review, section 6). Detail: the review, sections 1.8, 6, 7.1 and 8.

- F-350 **On the compiled path the arms of a parallel `do`, the elements of a tuple, the operands of an operator and the arguments of a call fork through one method, `CodeGen.genParallelExprs`, which joins every arm that it forked before an exception leaves the group; arguments fork where `ParallelismAnalyzer` marked the argument tuple.** The exception that leaves is that of the first arm, in the arms' order, that threw; when an exception leaves, an arm not yet forked is not run, and a `VirtualMachineError` leaves without the joins (`runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:113-131`, `joinIfForked`). The analyzer marks no call written in the prelude's files, so the prelude's reductions run in sequence until the switch-over (row 982); the one library's parallel `ZZ32` range splits only a range of more than `grainSize`, 16, elements (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:20`, `:1320`, `:1337`). What it means: compiled against the one library, a reduction over more than 16 elements will fork its halves, and an exception leaves no arm running. By reading, not run: microGPT's vectors are 16, 16, 4 and 4 wide (`explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:17`), so a reduction over one of them forks nothing on either path. Tests: `compiler_tests/AlsoArmThrowsJoinsCompiled`, `CallArgumentsForkCompiled`, `tests/ParRangeGrainWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-forked-arguments/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "Points to report reached"; the model's widths against the grain: `reviews/batch-30-review.md`, "2. The three forks that landed at a default".

- P-9 **The revival searches for the most readable expression of the microGPT algorithm.** C4 is the flat microGPT program (`explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss`), whose data layout follows Aaron Hsu's flat style of APL (P-29: C4 is not edited for speed before microGPT runs compiled). In C4, the polishing happens in the vocabulary, the array operations that the model's lines call: `FlatArrays.fss` beside C4, and what of it has moved into the standard library (P-27: what a program builds that a more mature library would hold goes into the library). P-87 holds the limit: the model's text is the notation, and a change to a model line is shown to the curator as a diff first. C4 is the target form of the APL microGPT program (`explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fss`): the APL program is written so that each of its lines expands into the line that C4 writes by hand. C4 writes its hyperparameters as tuple bindings, such as `(nEmbd, blockSize, nHead, headDim, vocabSize, bosId) = (16, 16, 4, 4, 27, 26)`, the form to which the APL sub-language (P-10) expands a strand assignment, APL's binding of several names at once. The one-line form, declarations separated by semicolons such as `nEmbd = 16; blockSize = 16; ...`, is not used: the APL sub-language has no use for it.

content.content:
### 1.6 The code generator's `atomic`

`forAtomicBlock` registers its exception-table entry before it emits the body (`CodeGen.java:1783`), so an outer block's handler precedes an inner one's (rows 934, 937; row 888 is the same for `try`). Its other gaps:

- It catches only `TransactionAbortException` (`:1780`), so a Fortress exception leaves the transaction pushed (row 324).
- It has no case for `AtomicExpr` or `TryAtomicExpr` (rows 875, 353).
- Mutable fields bypass the transaction (`VarCodeGen.java:209`, `:220`; row 319).

### 7.2 Known rows: confirmed or corrected

- **933, rewrite.** The claim is true but narrow. The mechanism also aborts a block, without any nesting, whenever any other block commits during it (§3.2). Proposed whole line:

  | 933 | on the compiled path a block that reads a variable it wrote records that write as a read, so it aborts whenever any block commits before it does, on any variable; after it commits a nested block, its next read aborts it every time, and it never ends | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (runtime) | `basic/expressions/atomic.tex`, "Atomic Expressions" | none | climb batch 28 rung A | `TXReadLocation` puts an own or ancestral write into the read set (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:223`, the team's text at a874948ac), and validation compares it with the committed value (`:247`, `:266-270`); a nested commit moves the global clock (`:306`, `:346`). `var x`, `var z`, `atomic do x := 2; y: ZZ32 = x; atomic do z := 1 end; w: ZZ32 = x end` under `timeout`: exit 124 at 157323e5, fe19fdad, f5aa647de. 20,000 blocks `x := x + 1; y := x` beside a task committing on `z` alone: 1,635 to 30,350 retries; the same writes without the read: 0. No gated test: the run step has no timeout (`tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:585`). |

- **934, 937: confirmed at f5aa647de.** `d 310, 337, 334` of 400 (934); `XXXNestedAtomicAbortCompiled` FAIL 3 of 3 (937). Their mechanism is the team's (§2). Both rows' notes are full (`ledger.py note … --check`: 3 characters left), so this confirmation lives here.
- **322, narrow the claim.** It holds only when the block ends an arm after the first. Arm 0 compiles in place (`CodeGen.java:1693`), and with the block there the probe printed PASS; in arm 1 it gave `VerifyError`. Proposed claim: "an `atomic do … end` block as the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm after the first produces a class that fails verification on the compiled path: `VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames at branch target 5`". The row has 96 characters left.
- **324: confirmed** at f5aa647de: `g = 7` compiled, `g = 100` under walk at 157323e5.
- **319: confirmed by reading.** `GETFIELD` and `PUTFIELD` with no check (`VarCodeGen.java:209`, `:220`).
- **59, 60: confirmed.** Unguarded counts are lost on both paths; reductions beside transactions are exact on both.
- **641: consistent.** 15 ns per plain increment of a top-level variable, including its two checks.
- **876: consistent by reading.** The unforked branch of `joinOrRun` never restores the current task (`BaseTask.java:148-149`).
- **82, 353, 497, 640, 888, 938, 417, 155, 265: not re-run.** They are consistent with the code read here.

### 7.3 Found by reading, no row drafted (decision 3)

- Walk's `ReadSet` copy constructor copies nothing (`ReadSet.java:29-42`; Java check above). Eager conflict detection masks it: the readers it drops are always ancestors of the new writer, which the writer relation protects. No program-level effect was found.
- `FException`'s static `HashMap` (§5): a data race and a leak, not reproduced.
- The racy retry tally (§3.3).
- `ParallelismAnalyzer`'s removal of the `FnDecl` instead of the name (§1.7).

## 8. The answer, in Pavol's terms

| block | verdict |
|---|---|
| fork/join pool and tasks, walk | **Mature enough.** Structured joins on every path; no grain size on `also`; `spawn` crude (a pool per spawn, spinning). |
| fork/join pool and tasks, compiled | **Sound core, immature edges.** It scales on private work (2.0–2.7×). It drops joins on abrupt completion (N1), relies on the current-task pointer (row 876), and runs call arguments, and so reductions, in sequence (N5). |
| library ranges and reductions | **Sound design.** Deterministic join trees, algebra by reduction objects, unchecked. Walk has no grain size; the compiled path runs reductions in sequence. |
| walk STM | **Mature for an interpreter, and faithful to the specification.** Strong atomicity, closed parallel nesting, a never-wait manager chosen for work stealing. One defect (N6); costly by design. |
| compiled STM | **An immature implementation of a sound algorithm family.** About two months old in 2012. Six runtime defects: rows 933 and 324's leak path, and N2, N3, N4, N7. No contention policy. It does not scale. |
| code generator's `atomic` | **Immature.** Rows 322, 324, 353, 875, 934, 937 and 319. |
| arrays inside transactions | walk: correct and costly. compiled: the `Object[]` slots are new (N7); unboxed stores have no transactional story (D1). |
| the language design | **Coherent, and fork/join plus STM is compatible in it.** Its flaws are of commitment, not contradiction: strong atomicity and parallel nesting are expensive; the programming discipline is unchecked; its gather tool, reduction variables, is unbuilt. |

So the mistakes found are signs of immature blocks, not of a broken design. The compiled path is where the immaturity sits. Two design-level gaps belong to the compiled implementation's choices, not to the language: weak atomicity (N2) and partial nested validation (N4).

**Repair before the compiled path relies on parallelism, in order:**
1. **N1.** Join every forked arm before a group completes abruptly, as walk does. Without it, an exception in parallel numeric code leaves writers running.
2. **N5,** with a grain size in the one library's parallel range. Without it, the model's reductions run in sequence.
3. **D1:** the unboxed store's stance on transactions, and its element access mode (opaque rather than volatile).
4. **Row 641's check** kept off, or hoisted out of, the unboxed element path.

**Before anything relies on `atomic`:**
- rows 933, 934/937/888 (one fix: register the handler after the body), 324, N4, N3 (per-task logs, or a lock on the shared sets), N7, 319 and 353;
- then D2 (strong atomicity) and a contention policy (backoff on, or a bound).

**Can wait:** walk's costs (P-29), the dead `ReadSet` copy, N6 (a nested `doItOnce` even inside a transaction would fix it), `spawn` (row 82), N8 (it goes with the prelude), the statistics, and sharedness and regions.

## Decisions

1. **Compiled probes in a worktree at main, repeated on the base for attribution.** Every new compiled defect reproduces on 157323e5. So N1–N6 and N8 are the team's code; N7 is batch 28's own line. The alternative, the base alone, would not have reached the slot API. No decision of the curator covers this; I followed the brief.
2. **The store's init race tested at Java level,** with `ArrayStoreJUTest`'s protocol, because no compiled program reaches the one library's arrays before the switch-over. The alternative, waiting for the switch-over, leaves A.skeptic.3 unmeasured.
3. **No rows for the four reading-only findings (§7.3).** None is reproduced as a program-level defect. The alternative was rows marked NEGATIVE-BOUNDED.
4. **A rewrite of row 933 rather than a sibling row.** It is one mechanism with two symptoms. The alternative is a new row, siblings 933.
5. **Timing only on the compiled path** (P-29), at one and four threads, alone on the machine.

## Questions for the curator (decisions not taken)

- **D1. Arrays of unboxed numbers and `atomic` (P-84, P-169).** P-169's own reason is that "a compiled atomic write into any array needs that keying". Today the slot API keys only `Object[]`, the `double[]` store "takes no part in a transaction", and N8 shows what an untracked store does under `atomic`. The options:
  - (a) Unboxed stores stay outside transactions. This is recorded as a departure in Appendix I. It contradicts P-169's reason.
  - (b) A primitive slot API, `TXReadDouble` and `TXWriteDouble`, validated by raw bits (NaN and -0.0 make `!=` wrong), plus a per-element check of about 1–2 ns (row 641's rate).
  - (c) The library checks once per bulk operation, `fill`, `map` or `mul`, and picks a transactional or a plain loop.

  There is no default on record. microGPT needs none of (b) or (c) for correctness.
- **D2. Strong atomicity on the compiled path** (N2; `atomic.tex:100-106`). The options:
  - (a) Keep weak atomicity for programs outside the discipline, recorded in Appendix I.
  - (b) Plain writes of mutable variables take the sequence lock: a compare-and-set pair per plain write.
  - (c) The specification's shared and local objects (`shared-local.tex`), so that only shared objects pay.

  Disciplined programs, microGPT among them, are unaffected by (a).
- **D3. Parallel reductions on the compiled path** (N5). The options:
  - (a) The code generator forks call arguments by `ParallelismAnalyzer`, as it does tuples.
  - (b) The one library's `generate` binds its halves as a tuple.
  - (c) Leave them sequential until PLAN's "compiled parallelism" (inventory B1 steps 20 and 21).

  This bears on PLAN's order.

## For FACTS

## 7. After the rehearsal's end (2026-11-10, 15:0x UTC)

The curator took option 3 of finding A: probes first, then the choice between options 1 and 2 (`coordinator/HELD.md`, the lines of 14:0x). The rehearsal's whole report is `compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/switch-rehearsal.md` at `d381e21775`. The pure-Java microGPT is timed in `java-baseline/python-comparison.md` at `1603d08b49`; its own report was not yet written. This section reads both. Below, A1 is finding A's option 1, the whole switch-over first, and A2 its option 2, the model's slice first.

### 7.1 What the rehearsal settled

- **A program runs compiled against the one library.** With 12 marked hacks, a program that prints a line, one that builds and reads an `Array1`, and a dot product in the program's own loop compile and run, with walk's output. So the first of the two unknowns of section 4.3 has its answer: yes, behind 14 walls.
- **No matrix runs, and none of the library's own array algebra.** Every array of rank 2 dies at `m[i,j]`: the method over the tuple index type has no body at the instantiated descriptor (its W15). The library's `DOT` and `SUM` die on a generic method that an object inherits from another component's trait (its W16). No hack passed either; each needs the code generator's real work. microGPT stops earlier, in the checker, with 17 sites of its own once `I extends Index` is written. That agrees with section 5.1 for `FlatArrays` (7 once the two bounds are written) and for `MicroGptFlat` (8). `FlatData` reads 1 there against 3 here: the compile command stops it at an error of `File`'s api, where the tolerant driver checks on.
- **Of the 16 walls, nine things are in no line of PLAN** (its section 6, last paragraph): the carrier design beyond N5's table, the team's search by the prelude's names in the trait table, the package in `OverloadSet`, `NN32`'s two getters, the methods written twice into 27 classes, the verifier's count over the emitted library, rows 624, 81 and 315 on the path of a one-line program, the tuple index type as the wall of every matrix, and the new library order of fourteen compiles.
- **The walls are of two kinds, and the kinds decide the sizes below.**
  - *Walls that a test against the prelude can show today.* They are the code generator's, each with a row whose reproducer runs in the prelude's world: varargs (row 624), `label` and `exit` (row 81), a closure class written twice (row 315), a method written twice with the wrong forwarder (row 571's kind), the missing cast at a `comprises` type (rows 307 and 695), the tuple index's bridge (row 832's kind), the inherited generic method (rows 495, 496, 732), and the rest of the 24 refused declarations (rows 822, 812, 819, 540, 875). ### 7.2 The sizes of A1 and A2 now

The unit is a batch with its landing, 5M to 14M tokens by the record. Phase 4 has landed at most three rungs that edit `CodeGen.java` in one batch (climb batch 30's record put a rung into its second run because the first "already has three rungs in `CodeGen.java`": `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-30.md`, "Why two runs"), so the 11 to 15 rungs of the first kind are 3 to 5 batches under either option. **A1, the whole switch-over first.**

1. The code generator's rungs that the prelude can test: 3 to 5 batches.
2. Then one landing that holds everything that only the switch shows, because, by the rehearsal's W2, the prelude's programs stop running once the value classes are re-parented: the carriers with the rungs around them, about seven in all, the verifier's count and what it finds, all 1,907 compiled tests moved or respelled, and the prelude's deletion. The record's bound for it was "at least two gated batches". The rehearsal met 16 walls on the way to three small programs, so 3 to 5 is the fairer range. It lands whole or not at all, and nothing in it is gated before it lands. The batch workflow has no form for it: a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, and these walls stand one behind the other.
3. The milestone: after 6 to 10 batches, 30M to 140M tokens. microGPT's own needs follow (the model's sized types, run-time sizes, `File` and `FileSupport`, the tuple binding, the numeral tie): 1 or 2 batches more.

**A2, the model's slice first.**

Beside them, in the same batches, since they touch other files: the carriers built as a second set of the thirteen value classes, chosen by the world that the compile command and the run select; the tables, the two converters and the 99 raise strings made to follow that choice; the rungs around them; a second library order and one test track against the one library in the gate. **What separates them.** Not the total: A2 is A1 plus two or three rungs, about 200 s more in every gate for the second library order, and a prelude that lives until the end. content.content:
## The manifest and the scatter

Per rung, the manifest gives:

- `id`, `slug`, `path` (its worktree), `branch` (`wip/<slug>`) and `title`;
- `blurb`, one line for the batch table every agent reads;
- `section`, the rung's section of the batch record word for word, which every role on the rung reads;
- `pointsToReport`, the kinds of change the curator reviews after the landing;
- `briefing`, the `facts-extract.sh` keys the worker reads first, with `reasons`, one line per key, rendered at the end of the worker's brief;
- `checks`, the sub-list of the briefing that the skeptic, a judge and a repair round read;
- `expectedMinutes`, which only orders the scatter;
- `writesState`, `testIsStage`, `gateJoins` (a gate step the rung brings, such as `testSpecData`), `expectedMoves` (ladder moves declared), and the optional `landsOnlyWith`, `expectedCheckerCount` and `expectedCheckerCrash`.

The script refuses at load a rung without its required fields, a key holding a double quote, backtick, dollar sign, backslash or newline (each is rendered in double quotes), a `checks` key not in the briefing, and `reasons` that are not one line per key.

The scatter starts the longest expected worker first. Two agents run at once on this box and a freed slot goes to the next queued agent (the `cloud-container` skill's `references/machine.md`, "The machine"), so the longest-first order saves up to the shortest worker's time at the end. The gather keeps the manifest's order for its own reading and applies the rungs in its own order (below).

`landsOnlyWith` names the rungs a rung lands only with. After the scatter, a rung any of whose named rungs is not approved is withheld, repeated until nothing moves; it reaches the gather as not landed, and its expected moves and checker declarations stop counting at the gate. Batch 6's T, the number chapters, landed only with F, the flat library they describe. The gather applies such a rung after the rungs it names ("Gather", "The order").

### The disk before the scatter

Before the scatter, one agent runs `df -P /home/user` and returns what it printed; the script reads the Available column itself (the `cloud-container` skill's `references/machine.md`, "The disk allowance": Size misleads, Available is what is left). Under the floor, 1.5 G a rung plus 4 G for the main tree (`DISK_FLOOR_G`; 19 G for ten rungs), or with no line of its output to read (an agent that returns nothing after its three attempts among them), the run stops with a message that gives the figure, the floor and the line, before any rung starts. The coordinator frees disk and launches the batch again with the same args: a new launch, not `resumeFromRunId`, whose journal would return the same reading. On a resume after a later stop, the first reading comes back from the journal and the disk is not read again. The ground of the floor: a rung worktree is seeded at about 206 MB and grew to 0.28 to 1.1 G in climb batch 27 (`du -sh` in its agents' transcripts), and the main tree's stages write the gather's builds and demos, the gate's results and the ladder's two copies of the caches, and the specification's build. Climb batch 27 started its ten rungs without that margin: the allowance ran out, 31 MB to 443 MB free through the batch, rungs S and T never started, and other stages skipped their measures (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/RECORD.md`, "Not landed"; `PLAN.md` item 68). Scenarios K1 and K2.

## What a batch commits

A batch commits on a `wip/` branch what it commits on `main`, and nothing else. That is the Fortress change (source, library, specification text, tests) and its reports: `REPORT.md`, `SKEPTIC.md`, `JUDGE.md`, a decision record where the section asks for one, and the batch's `RECORD.md`. It also commits the ledger rows, the FACTS, PLAN and handover lines, each rung's revival-change material in the batch's `RECORD.md`, and a script that is reusable. It commits nothing under `.claude/`: only the skill writer edits the skills (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`). No captured output, log, probe program or copy of a script is committed. An agent's scratch lives under its worktree's `tmp/`, which git ignores and which goes with the worktree, never in the session's scratchpad, which every agent of a run shares: every brief's head says so, since in climb batch 24 eight of the 18 agents wrote files there, and two skeptics one file name (`reviews/batch-24-review.md`, finding 8). Whether a worker wrote its test first and saw it fail is read in its transcript, which the backup keeps (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "While it runs"; `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md`, "What to commit").

## Preparing a batch record

An Opus planning worker drafts `CLIMB-BATCH-<n>.md`. A Fable reviewer edits it in place with one reason per change. The coordinator reads the diff and brings the record's questions to the curator one per message. The batch launches on the answers or on the standing go (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The go").

The planner builds each rung's briefing as in-context learning: the agents were not trained on Fortress, and the language was never finished (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). A briefing holds what the rung's section cites: the decisions and earlier rulings it rests on, its ledger rows, the specification's sections whole by their headings, the notes on the subject by section, and the library code that is the precedent. Process positions and harness facts stay out, because the brief's role text and the skill carry them. In batch 10 the workers named none of the 87 POSITIONS and FACTS keys before their fix edits (`process-engineering/context-study.md`, section 5). Each key goes through `facts-extract.sh --check` on the base, every key matching exactly one place. Each carries one line on why it is there. The planner marks the `checks` sub-list: the decisions and rows the checks need, and the sections and precedent code they compare against.

A rung that changes what an implementation does is briefed with the Appendix I Effects and the specification's notes that its change makes false, found by a grep while the record is prepared. Batch 9's record gave rung K none, and Appendix I's `comprises` Effect was that batch's one blocking finding (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, finding 3).

A record asks a rung for no corpus-wide output comparison, no ladder before-run, no microGPT check and no specification build log (P-103, "The suite's verdict is the check."; the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "What a brief holds"). Whole suites are the skill's rule (`tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). A count of the programs a change reaches, when a decision needs one, is the planner's probe, taken before the record is written. A named one-time count of changed outputs is asked only where a decision of the curator's names it for that rung. The coordinator starts its base pass before the launch (`tools/count-run/count-run.sh`).

A ledger note that the record briefs fits its row: the planner reads the row with `ledger.py show N` against the tool's limits (notes 700 characters, the row 1,200) and, where the note does not fit, briefs the row's whole new line. Climb batch 26's record briefed rung S a note to row 440, whose notes held 676 of 700 characters (`reviews/batch-26-review.md`, process finding 6).

The record's section on how it is run gives the manifest's fields rung by rung, the intro every agent reads, and the launch steps. It holds no copy of the block: the batch's generator writes the block from the record.

## Before the launch

The coordinator, in this order:

1. The script, this manual and the batch's manifest generator on `main`. The base is `main`'s head after them, by its full hash, passed as `args.base`.
2. The batch's one base build, a worktree at the base outside the main tree, built once and then left alone. Every rung worktree is seeded from it, and the old code runs from it (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). About 200 s, as the skill's `worktrees.md`, "Finding or building a base build", gives it:

        git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add --detach /home/user/fortress-base<N> <base>
        cd /home/user/fortress-base<N>      # then set up the call as the skill's build-and-caches.md says
        ant compileAll                      # BUILD SUCCESSFUL
        # the library order (build-and-caches.md, "The library order"), then one walk run, which warms walk's caches:
        bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
        git status --porcelain              # empty: the seed refuses a base build that is not clean

   Its path goes to the launch as `args.baseBuild`. The script refuses to start without it (scenario B1).
3. One trial seed proves the base build, about 3 s: `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck - <base>`, then `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-seedcheck`. One `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck-caches ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, run from the main tree, proves the old code runs; its folder is removed after.
4. The briefings checked on the base (`python3 explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/manifest/lists<N>.py`). The block generated (`gen<N>.py`), checked in a scratch copy and spliced (`check<N>.js`, then `check<N>.js --write`). Then `node explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` on the spliced script, which also checks that every skill section the script cites by name is a heading of the skill. Then the commit.
5. `df -P /home/user`, its Available column at or above the script's floor, 1.5 G a rung plus 4 G ("The disk before the scatter"), which the script reads again before the scatter and stops under. `git status --porcelain` empty in the main tree, and no other agent writing there or pushing `main` while the run gathers and commits. The session's permission rules let the commit stage run `tools/mg-run.sh`.
6. Check-ins armed for the run's length, 45 minutes apart (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "Watching a run").

The launch: `Workflow({scriptPath: 'explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js', args: {base: '<full hash>', baseBuild: '/home/user/fortress-base<N>'}})`. The args are kept byte for byte, since a resume needs them. The base build stays until the coordinator removes it after the landing.

## Gather

The gather composes one local commit per approved rung on `main`; nothing is merged.

- **The order.** First, a rung goes after every rung it lands only with (`landsOnlyWith`), so that no commit on `main` holds a rung without the rungs it needs: in climb batch 17 the old rule, which compared lines across files, put rung L's `2b1cd8e63` before rung W's `743eb5286`, and that commit alone fails `LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss:37` (`reviews/batch-17-review.md`, finding 2). Then the rungs that share a file go in the ascending order of their lowest edited line in that file, so that a later hunk does not shift lines a landed record cites; a line is compared only with a line of the same file, and rungs that share no file keep the manifest's order. Where two files order one pair both ways, the pair keeps the manifest's order. Any `file:line` a record cites that an earlier hunk shifted is re-anchored by symbol. Tests cite the specification by section, never by line, so no test is re-anchored.
- **Each rung.** Its net diff is applied with `git apply --3way --index`. A conflict in unrelated regions is resolved by hand; one in the same logic is returned, not guessed. Its files are written from the journal where the branch lacks them, by the commands the brief renders per rung. For a repaired rung, `REPORT.md` and `record.md` are always rewritten from the repair round's texts.
- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there").
- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
- **After the rungs.** The landed rungs' walk tests run on the merged tree in one `harness-one.sh` call, each `X.test` named beside its `X.fss`: climb batch 26's gather ran its 20 twice, the first call without the five `.test` files (`reviews/batch-26-review.md`, process finding 7). One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). A row whose test is the checker count or the distance stage closes on the rung's run of it, the gate's tables its check: the gather runs neither stage. In climb batch 25 it ran the distance stage for row 873 on code the gate measured again (`reviews/batch-25-review.md`, finding 6). One commit writes the batch's `RECORD.md`, once, last: the order and why, each rung's commit, the rows opened and closed, each skeptic's fixes and the contested rulings by commit, the rungs that did not land, the points to report, where each item for the curator went, and last, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer", each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both parts word for word.
- **The specification's PDF.** When the gather builds the specification to check its text, it builds it once, on the text after the last edit under `Specification/`, and keeps the PDF at `tmp/gather/fortress-batch-<N>.pdf` in the main tree, which the commit stage takes ("Commit, and the push held", step 1).

A rung that did not land has its `REPORT.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` taken out of its branch path by path, its findings folded under "Not landed", and its new rows added. None of its source is applied.

Files are staged by an explicit list and `git diff --cached --stat` is read before each commit. A commit touching a path outside `explorations/` and `.claude/` carries a `historical:` line.

IDS = tuple(r for r in ORDER if _B[r])
assert all([e[0] for e in _B[r]].count(FORKS_SECTION) == 1 for r in IDS), 'each briefing names the forks once'


def lists(ids=IDS):
    """(LISTS, REASONS) for the rungs ids: LISTS[r] is (briefing keys, checks keys), REASONS[r] the (key, reason) pairs."""
    assert all(r in IDS for r in ids), ids
    out_l, out_r = {}, {}
    for r in ids:
        es = [(e[0], e[1], len(e) > 2 and e[2]) for e in _B[r]]
        out_l[r] = ([k for k, _, _ in es], [k for k, _, c in es if c])
        out_r[r] = [(k, why) for k, why, _ in es]
    return out_l, out_r


LISTS, REASONS = lists(IDS)


def reason_problems(rid, reasons=None):
    out = []
    for k, r in (reasons or REASONS)[rid]:
        if not r or not r.strip():
            out.append((k, 'no reason'))
        elif '\n' in r or '`' in r or any(ord(c) > 127 for c in r):
            out.append((k, 'a reason is one ASCII line with no backtick'))
        elif not r.endswith('.') or len(r) > 240:
            out.append((k, 'a reason ends with a full stop and is at most 240 characters'))
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    import subprocess, re, sys
    root = _ROOT
    bad = 0
    print('tree', root)
    run = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--run') + 1] if '--run' in sys.argv else None

    CHECKED = RUNS[run] if run else IDS
    print('rungs', ', '.join(CHECKED), '(run ' + run + ')' if run else '(both runs)')

    def check(keys):
        r = subprocess.run(['bash', 'explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh', '--check'] + list(keys), capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=root)
        return r, [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\[([0-9]+) bytes\]', r.stdout)]
    for rid in CHECKED:
        b, c = LISTS[rid]
        rp = reason_problems(rid)
        print(rid, 'reasons', len(REASONS[rid]), 'for', len(b), 'briefing keys |', 'problems', len(rp))
        for k, why in rp: print('   PROBLEM', why, ':', k[:200])

        for name, keys in (('briefing', b), ('checks', c)):
            if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
                print('   PROBLEM duplicate key in', rid, name); bad += 1

            if badk:
                print('   PROBLEM keys the script refuses', rid, name, badk); bad += 1
            if name == 'checks':
                stray = [k for k in keys if k not in b]
                if stray:
                    print('   PROBLEM checks keys not in the briefing', rid, stray); bad += 1
            r, _ = check(keys)
            lines = r.stdout.strip().splitlines()
            probs = [l for l in lines if 'not one' in l or 'NOT FOUND' in l or 'no match' in l.lower() or 'no line of' in l or 'no such file' in l]
            total = [l for l in lines if l.startswith('Total')]
            print(rid, name, 'keys', len(keys), 'exit', r.returncode, '|', total[0] if total else r.stderr.strip()[:200])
            for l in probs: print('   PROBLEM', l[:300])
            if r.returncode or probs:
                bad += 1
                if os.environ.get('VERBOSE'): print(r.stdout)
        # The forks key alone: what the rung reads of section 3.
        fk = [k for k in b if k == FORKS_SECTION]

        total = [l for l in r.stdout.strip().splitlines() if l.startswith('Total')]

        if r.returncode or len(sizes) != len(fk) or len(fk) != 1:
            print('   PROBLEM the forks key is not held once, or matches no one place'); bad += 1
    print('bad lists', bad)
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

# Made from plan-29b/manifest/gen29b.py for climb batch 30, whose record holds two runs, as CLIMB-BATCH-21.md did
# (plan-21/manifest/gen21.py): run 1, climb batch 30, the rungs N, P and X; run 2, climb batch 30b, the rungs Y and C,
# written on run 1's landed tree. --run 1|2 chooses the block: its BATCH (30 or 30b, so the script's BATCH_DIR is
# compile-ladder/climb-batch-30/ or climb-batch-30b/), its rungs from lists30.RUNS in the manifest's order, and its
# part of the intro. --without <rung> leaves a rung of that run out of the block. A rung's section runs from its
# heading to the next ### heading, as check30.js reads it.
# Changed from gen29b.py: the batch's values (the record CLIMB-BATCH-30.md for both runs, the lists lists30.py, the
# output manifest30.js or manifest30b.js under $OUT30); section 1's table has a run column, which must agree with
# lists30.RUNS; the "Fields common to the five rungs": no rung lands only with another ("lands only with: none"), the
# joins-the-gate field gives none but the specification's build at the gather of each run, no rung declares a count,
# a crash or a move; a table title is the rung's short name and need not open its section 4 heading, which is the
# block's title; the intro is the part of section 6's "What every agent reads first" led by "Run 1." or "Run 2.",
# without that lead. P and C name the count stage and the distance stage in a step of their sections, C with P-148's
# runs; N, X and Y say "The stages. None" and list their files (section 1's common fields; section 6, "The
# generator"): check30.js checks them. Each briefing's forks are the record's one forks key, section 3's "Forks the
# batch takes" whole, for every rung (lists30.py's header). Run 2's block is generated again after its sections are
# re-read against run 1's landed tree (the record's section 4).
# Generates the MANIFEST block for the batch workflow (explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js;
# explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/batch-redesign.md) from the record, read at run time, and the
# briefings of lists30.py, into $OUT30/manifest30.js or manifest30b.js ($FORTRESS_HOME/tmp by default, which is
# ignored); check30.js checks it and splices it. On batch 15's pattern (plan-15/manifest/gen15.py): each rung's
# section of the record's section 4 goes into the block word for word as the rung's section, which every role on the
# rung reads (the worker, the skeptic, a judge and a repair round), its code-span backticks dropped, any ellipsis
# character written as three full stops and any minus sign as a hyphen-minus; the briefing's reasons go beside the
# keys, and the script renders them at the end of the worker's brief. No value is set at launch: the gather numbers
# the batch's new rows through ledger.py, so the block has no LEDGER_FROM.
#   python3 -B gen30.py --run 1|2 [--without <rung>]... [RECORD]   RECORD defaults to explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-30.md
import json, re, sys, os
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from lists30 import lists, IDS as ALL_IDS, RUNS

ROOT = os.environ.get('FORTRESS_HOME', os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '../../../..')))
argv = sys.argv[1:]
assert '--run' in argv and argv[argv.index('--run') + 1] in RUNS, 'usage: gen30.py --run 1|2 [--without <rung>]... [RECORD]'
RUN = argv[argv.index('--run') + 1]
del argv[argv.index('--run'):argv.index('--run') + 2]
RUN_IDS = RUNS[RUN]
WITHOUT = []
while '--without' in argv:
    WITHOUT.append(argv[argv.index('--without') + 1])
    del argv[argv.index('--without'):argv.index('--without') + 2]
args = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith('--')]
assert all(w in RUN_IDS for w in WITHOUT), ('--without names a rung not in the run', WITHOUT)
IDS = tuple(r for r in RUN_IDS if r not in WITHOUT)
LISTS, REASONS = lists(IDS)
BATCH = {'1': '30', '2': '30b'}[RUN]
BATCH_RECORD = 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-30.md'
BRIEFING_LISTS = 'explorations/compile-ladder/plan-30/manifest/lists30.py'
REC = args[0] if args else os.path.join(ROOT, BATCH_RECORD)
OUT = os.path.join(os.environ.get('OUT30', os.path.join(ROOT, 'tmp')), 'manifest%s.js' % BATCH)
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
rec = open(REC, encoding='utf-8').read()
# The characters outside ASCII that a section may keep, each written as a \u escape by js(): none in this batch.
KEPT = ''


def ascii_text(t, keep=''):
    t = t.replace('`', '').replace('…', '...').replace('−', '-')
    bad = [c for c in t if ord(c) > 127 and c not in keep]
    assert not bad, ('non-ASCII left', bad, t[:120])
    return t


def between(text, start, end):
    i = text.index(start)
    j = text.index(end, i + len(start))
    return text[i + len(start):j]


# Section 4: one block per rung, from its heading to the next ### heading, each opening with "The mission.".
s4 = between(rec, '\n## 4. The rungs\n', '\n## 5. ')
heads = list(re.finditer(r'^### ([A-Z])\. (.*)$', s4, flags=re.M))
assert [h.group(1) for h in heads] == list(ALL_IDS), [h.group(1) for h in heads]
sections, titles, headings = {}, {}, {}
for i, h in enumerate(heads):
    rid = h.group(1)
    nxt = re.search(r'^### ', s4[h.end():], flags=re.M)
    end = h.end() + nxt.start() if nxt else len(s4)
    body = s4[h.end():end].strip('\n')
    paras = body.split('\n\n')
    assert paras[0].startswith('**The mission.**'), (rid, 'the section does not open with The mission.')
    headings[rid] = ascii_text(rid + '. ' + h.group(2))
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    sections[rid] = ascii_text(body, KEPT)
    titles[rid] = ascii_text(h.group(2))

# Section 1: the table, the fields common to the five rungs, and each rung's block.
s1 = between(rec, '\n## 1. The manifest, rung by rung\n', '\n## 2. ')
table = {}
for line in s1.split('\n'):
    m = re.match(r'^\| ([12]) \| ([A-Z]) \| `([a-z0-9-]+)` \| (.*) \| ([0-9]+) \|$', line)
    if m:
        table[m.group(2)] = {'run': m.group(1), 'slug': m.group(3), 'title': ascii_text(m.group(4)), 'minutes': int(m.group(5))}
assert list(table) == list(ALL_IDS), list(table)
assert all(r in RUNS[table[r]['run']] for r in ALL_IDS), ('the table\'s run column and lists30.RUNS differ', {r: table[r]['run'] for r in ALL_IDS})
common_text = between(s1, '\nFields common to the five rungs:\n', '\n### ')
COMMON = {}
for m in re.finditer(r'\*\*([a-z ]+):\*\* ([^.;:]*)', common_text):
    COMMON[m.group(1)] = ascii_text(m.group(2).strip())
# The specification's build runs at the gather of each run, not in the gate: no rung brings a gate step.
assert re.fullmatch(r"none(, but the specification's build at the gather of each run, for N's and C's text)?", COMMON.get('joins the gate', '')), ('common field', 'joins the gate', COMMON.get('joins the gate'))
want_common = {'writes state': 'no', 'its test is the stage': 'no', 'expected moves': 'none', 'lands only with': 'none',
               'expected checker count': 'none declared', 'expected checker crash': 'none'}
for k, v in want_common.items():
    assert COMMON.get(k) == v, ('common field', k, COMMON.get(k))


def rung_names(text):
    """'N, C, F and S' -> ['N', 'C', 'F', 'S']."""
    names = [x.strip() for x in re.split(r',\s*|\s+and\s+', text.strip().rstrip('.')) if x.strip()]
    assert all(re.fullmatch(r'[A-Z]', x) for x in names), ('not a list of rungs', text)
    return names


# The common lands-only-with field: "none. In each run every rung lands on its own." No rung's block has one.
assert re.search(r'^- \*\*lands only with:\*\* none\. In each run every rung lands on its own\.', common_text, flags=re.M), 'the common lands-only-with field'
COMMON_LOW = {}
blocks = list(re.finditer(r'^### ([A-Z])$', s1, flags=re.M))
assert [b.group(1) for b in blocks] == list(ALL_IDS), [b.group(1) for b in blocks]
FIELDS = {}
for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
    rid = b.group(1)
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    text = s1[b.end():blocks[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(blocks) else len(s1)]
    f, points, in_points = {}, [], False
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        m = re.match(r'^- \*\*([a-z ]+):\*\*\s*(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
            in_points = (key == 'points to report')
            if not in_points:
                f[key] = ascii_text(val)
            continue
        if line.startswith('- **briefing**'):
            in_points = False
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^  - (.*)$', line)
        if m and in_points:
            points.append(ascii_text(m.group(1).strip()))
    f['points'] = points
    for k in ('slug', 'worktree', 'section', 'blurb'):
        assert k in f, (rid, k)
    assert points, (rid, 'no points to report')
    assert f['slug'] == table[rid]['slug'], (rid, 'slug differs from the table')
    assert f['worktree'] == '/home/user/fortress-' + re.sub(r'^rung-', '', f['slug']), (rid, 'worktree', f['worktree'])
    assert f['section'] == headings[rid], (rid, 'section field differs from the section 4 heading', f['section'], headings[rid])
    f['expected minutes'] = table[rid]['minutes']
    assert not any(k.startswith('waits on') for k in f), (rid, 'a waits-on line, which no rung of this batch has')
    # A rung's own "lands only with" field, which the common field must give alike; none where neither names it.
    own = rung_names(re.sub(r'\s*\(.*?\)\.?$', '', f['lands only with'])) if 'lands only with' in f else []
    assert own == COMMON_LOW.get(rid, []), (rid, 'its lands-only-with field and the common one differ', own, COMMON_LOW.get(rid))
    f['lands only with'] = own
    assert all(x in RUN_IDS and x != rid for x in own), (rid, own)
    FIELDS[rid] = f
s6 = rec[rec.index('\n## 6. How it is run\n'):]
intros = between(s6, '\n### What every agent reads first\n', '\n### Before the launch\n').strip()
# The run's part: from its lead, "**Run 1.**" or "**Run 2.**", to the other run's lead or the end, without the lead.
leads = {r: intros.index('**Run %s.** ' % r) for r in RUNS}
assert leads['1'] == 0 and leads['2'] > 0, 'the intro opens with Run 1. and holds Run 2.'
intro = (intros[:leads['2']] if RUN == '1' else intros[leads['2']:])[len('**Run %s.** ' % RUN):].strip()
assert intro.startswith('This run is climb batch %s, ' % BATCH), intro[:80]
INTRO = ascii_text(intro)


def js(x):
    return json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=True)


def js_list(keys, indent='      '):
    out, cur = [], ''
    for k in keys:
        piece = js(k)
        if cur and len(cur) + len(piece) + 2 > 150:
            out.append(indent + cur.rstrip())
            cur = ''
        cur += piece + ', '
    if cur:
        out.append(indent + cur.rstrip().rstrip(','))
    return '\n'.join(out)

    assert re.fullmatch(r'[a-z0-9-]+', slug), slug
    path = f['worktree']
    assert re.fullmatch(r'/home/user/fortress-[a-z0-9-]+', path), path
    A("const %s_ENTRY = { id: '%s', slug: '%s', path: '%s', branch: 'wip/%s', expectedMinutes: %d," % (rid, rid, slug, path, slug, f['expected minutes']))

for line in L:

open(OUT, 'w').write(BLOCK)
print('run', RUN, 'batch', BATCH, 'wrote', OUT, len(L), 'lines')

## The atomic runs

The atomic runs compile twenty-two programs, and run each one three times at four threads. They need the library's jars in the tree's caches (`build-and-caches.md`). Run them from `ProjectFortress/`:

    for p in AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG \
             AlsoArmThrowsJoinsCompiled CallArgumentsForkCompiled AtomicOwnWriteNestedCompiled \
             AtomicNestedSameBodyCompiled NestedAtomicAbortCompiled AtomicNestedViewCompiled \
             AtomicSharedReadsCompiled AtomicThrowRevertsCompiled \
             atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 \
             nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2 ; do
      d=other_compiler_tests ; [ -f compiler_tests/$p.fss ] && d=compiler_tests
      timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile $d/$p.fss >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" ; continue ; }
      for i in 1 2 3 ; do
        out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$?
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && { out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$? ; }
        case "$out" in *FAIL*) r=FAIL ;; *PASS*) r=PASS ;; *) r="NO-PASS rc=$rc" ;; esac
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && r=TIMEOUT-TWICE
        echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 $r"
      done
    done

The gate is red on any FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE.

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

content.content:
## 2. A line of the model that the checker refuses against the one library

`MicroGptFlat.fss:82` is `learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)`. The checker refuses `1.0 s`:

    Ambiguous coercion in call to operator juxtaposition: of the declarations applicable to an argument of type
    (RadixPointNumeral[\2,1,10,10\], ZZ32) only by coercion, none is more specific than every other:
    ((RR64 & {Float}), RR64)->RR64; (QQ, QQ)->QQ.

`model-closure/NumeralLine.fss` pins it in three lines (`1.0 s`, `(1.0 s) / 2` and the model's line), each refused. The two declarations differ at the numeral's place and at the `ZZ32`'s, so the rule for declarations tied only at numerals does not reach it. Walk runs the line at `RR64`. No compiled test meets it today, since the prelude has no `QQ`. It is also the form that the `fortress-repo` skill advises for a float quotient (`references/revival-changes.md`, "`/` on two integers answers a `QQ`").

## 3. The model's hyperparameter lines do not compile under either library
component NumeralLine
export Executable
lr0: RR64 = 0.01
nSteps: ZZ32 = 1000
learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)
half(s: ZZ32): RR64 = (1.0 s) / 2
scaled(s: ZZ32): RR64 = 1.0 s
run(): () = println learningRate(3)
end

# The check of climb batch 31's record, before the launch

## 1. For the curator

**What this is.** Climb batch 31 is a plan for seven changes to the compiler, in two runs. It has no go from you. I read the plan as a stranger and checked it against the code and against your decisions. I changed no design.

**The words.**

- **Walk** is the interpreter. The **compiled path** is the compiler: its **checker** checks types, its **code generator** writes Java bytecode.
- The **prelude** is the compiler's own small library. The **one library** is the interpreter's library, which the compiler must learn to compile.
- A **rung** is one change, built by one worker. A **reproducer** is a small program that shows a defect. A worker must see its test fail before it repairs anything.
- A **numeral** is a number written in digits, such as `0`.

**What I checked.**

- Every file, line, ledger row and decision that the plan cites.
- Every reproducer, run once on today's code.
- Every rung against your decisions.
- Whether four workers can edit the code generator's main file in one run.
- The plan's way of counting progress.

**What I found.**

- **The plan is sound in its main lines.** Eleven of its twelve reproducers fail today exactly as the plan says. Its citations hold, with eight small corrections.
- **One step has no failing test.** Rung L has two halves. Its first half, `label` and `exit`, is fine. Its second half gives each closure class a name of its own. A closure is a function written inside an expression. The plan says that two old programs show this defect. I ran both. Both compile and run today. So a worker cannot see that test fail first. The defect is real in the one library, but nobody has a small program that shows it. This should be settled before the launch: either a short probe finds such a program, or that half waits.
- **Your one question, fork W, is the right question.** It asks whether walk gets the new numeral rule now, or later. Now is way (a). Later is way (b). I agree that only you can answer it. I corrected one sentence in it. Details below.
- **No other fork needs you.** I checked all seventeen by the rule. One, fork N2, comes nearest: it lets two lines of microGPT compile unchanged. Your decision P-173 already covers it.
- **Four workers in one file can be merged.** Each keeps to its own part of the file. Three places need a word from the coordinator first. None needs you.

**Fork W, what each way leaves different between walk and the compiler.**

- **Way (a), walk now.** `u = 0` is `true` on both. One new difference appears. Take a variable declared with the widest type, `a: Any`, that holds a zero of type `NN32`. Walk will say `a = 0` is `true`. The compiler will say `false`. Today both say `false`. The plan said that this difference "stays". It does not exist today, so I wrote "appears".
- **Way (b), walk waits.** `u = 0` stays `false` under walk and `true` when compiled, as today. The same holds for `u =/= 0`, for `case u of 0`, and for a program's own number type. These are four known defects that stay open until walk runs the checker. The `a: Any` case stays the same on both.

### B2. An `exit` out of an `atomic` block has no owner

The specification: "If it completes abruptly by exiting to an enclosing `label` expression, writes within the block are retained and become visible to other threads" (`Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:60-63`). The compiled handler takes every exception and ends the transaction, "whose writes go with it" (`runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:285-314`; F-351).
